pr_body:
Log events when a ServiceProvider is created:

* How many singleton, scoped, transient services?
* Log the list of registrations

Fix #56313

Of the list in #56313, I left out `How many container instances are in the processes?` because this can be determined from the number of `ServiceProviderBuilt` events that have occurred in the process.

issue_context.title: Additional Diagnostics in Dependency Injection
issue_context.body:
The goal is to help customers better understand how their applications are running by adding events and counters that can give more insights and will help them debug potential performance issues. It'll also help us debug customer applications and write tools that would be able to glean insights from traces.

We would like to help customers better understand some statistics about registered services:
* How many singleton services?
* How many scoped services?
* How many transient services?
* How many container instances are in the processes?

@davidfowl - were you thinking that all 4 of the above would be "counters" (for example how many times services were resolved). Or do you think a single event during `BuildServiceProvider` that logs how many singleton, scoped, and transient service types?

Initially I was thinking counters but now I'm thinking event because they don't change throughout the lifetime of the app. 

Also we need to add service provider instance id to the event and existing events since many can exists in the application (like in orchard)

> but now I'm thinking event because they don't change throughout the lifetime of the app.

So you are thinking the count of types, and not the count of instances. Right?

> add service provider instance id to the event and existing events

I assume adding info to an existing event isn't considered a "breaking change"

> So you are thinking the count of types, and not the count of instances. Right?

Correct, instances can be found using an allocation profiler.

> I assume adding info to an existing event isn't considered a "breaking change"

That's right.
I'm also thinking we should dump the list of registrations

review_comments: Generally speaking, the pattern is to do less string formatting and to do more writing of events with payloads that can then be processed out-of-proc.  This looks like it might be a place where building up the state in-proc is preferred, or that you have to string-ify things anyway, but just wanted to call that out.  Definitely good that this is under its own keyword.

Yeah, here we want to dump a bunch of data - the list of registered DI services. We are doing something similar above already:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a1aeb132ca60becb1e8ffe02150d59782c1214c2/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection/src/DependencyInjectionEventSource.cs#L80-L94

```suggestion
		[NonEvent]
        private static void AppendServiceDescriptor(StringBuilder builder, ServiceDescriptor descriptor)
``` #Closed

I think you might need to specify a keyword for the other events in this provider now.  If you turn on keyword 0x1, you'll just get the ServiceProviderInitialized events.  If you specify keyword 0, I'm not sure you'll get the others - worth checking via ETW.

>  If you turn on keyword 0x1, you'll just get the ServiceProviderInitialized events.

That was my intention. The existing events all check for `EventKeywords.All`:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/a1aeb132ca60becb1e8ffe02150d59782c1214c2/src/libraries/Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection/src/DependencyInjectionEventSource.cs#L80-L82

So if you don't specify `All`, you won't get those events.

> If you specify keyword 0, I'm not sure you'll get the others - worth checking via ETW.

When I do

```
dotnet trace collect --providers Microsoft-Extensions-DependencyInjection:0:Verbose --name OrchardCoreTest
```

I don't get any events logged.

When I do

```
 dotnet trace collect --providers Microsoft-Extensions-DependencyInjection::Verbose --name OrchardCoreTest
```

I get them all.

And when I do

```
dotnet trace collect --providers Microsoft-Extensions-DependencyInjection:1:Verbose --name OrchardCoreTest
```

I just get the 2 new ones.
